### The calculator asks for each scheme's own inputs (CG, RJ, UP, AP)

`feature` · `SUBS-002` `SUBS-003` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-15--feature--SUBS-002--each-schemes-own-inputs.md)

#### Before

Each system in `GET /subsidy/config` lists the extra request fields it needs, in `inputs`. The handover says to build the form from them, never from the state (`state-subsidy-formulas.md`, `andhra-pradesh-subsidy.md`). The calculator read none of them, so:

- CG, RJ and UP couldn't calculate. Sprinklers had no set size; CG and RJ drip had no spacing label; RJ had no filters or existing equipment.
- **An AP drip result failed outright:** the backend sends `regular_matrix_id: null` for it, and the response schema took only a string, so the whole calculation became a contract error.
- **New result rows were dropped:** CG's `fittings` and `flat_inspection`, AP's `gst_paid_by_state`, and RJ's unit-cost `add_ons` and `deductions` disappeared silently.
- **The scheme picker** sent no scheme for whichever active scheme came first in code order. "AP" sorts before "GGRC", so choosing AP calculated under Gujarat.

#### Now

- **"The scheme's inputs"** shows, under the head unit, what the system's config lists:
  - a sprinkler set size, 63, 75, 90 or 110 mm (`pipe_size_mm`);
  - a spacing from the scheme's own list (`spacing_label`, from `spacing_labels`);
  - RJ's hydrocyclone and gravel filter (none or a size), and "Farmer already has a head unit" and "… the PVC main line";
  - AP drip's "Guided cost (from the AP MIP portal)" and "Fittings and accessories (from the portal)", with "Copy these, and the lines above, from the portal's bill of quantities."
- A scheme that asks for none, Gujarat today, shows no card and sends exactly what it sent before. An input code the screen doesn't know yet is named in a note rather than ignored.
- **Before sending:** the figures wait for a required input ("Fill in the scheme's inputs to see the subsidy"). A spacing not in the scheme's list, or a money amount that isn't a number, is marked on its field. A backend refusal of any of these lands on its field too.
- **The results:**
  - an AP drip result reads with null matrix ids, and its figure is labelled "Guided cost (the portal's total)";
  - the summary adds "Fittings add-on", "Inspection charge (outside the cap)" and "GST paid by the state" wherever a column isn't zero;
  - RJ's unit cost says what the filters added and what the existing equipment took off.
- **New warnings have titles:** no rate for the set size, a subsidy above the cost, deductions above the unit cost, the pipe size ignored, the guided cost above the cost, the fittings amount above the lines, and an area between table steps.
- **The scheme picker** treats the backend's default, GGRC, as "none", and sends any other scheme by code, wherever it sorts.
- **The mock** lists each state's `inputs` by scheme code (CG, RJ, UP, AP), with invented spacing labels. It refuses a listed input that's missing, and AP's fields on another scheme. It calculates AP drip without a unit cost table, adding the state's half of the GST. Its AP figures are illustrative, not AP's formula.
- Checked on a desktop in light mode and a phone in dark mode: an AP scheme set up in Subsidy masters, then an AP drip quotation before and after the portal's figures. axe found nothing.

#### Discussion

- **Please confirm with the backend:** the AP handover asks whether the frontend is fine with `regular_matrix_id` and `seven_year_matrix_id` becoming nullable (breaking under ADR-028). This PR reads them as nullable and doesn't otherwise use them, so yes.
- **One crop and free-text crop names outside Gujarat:** the config's `crop_count_max` already limits the blocks to one. The crop is still chosen from `GET /subsidy/crops`, which serves each scheme's own list.
- **The quotation PDF and the farmer's link** still print without the state's GST for AP; that is the backend's GAP-482.
- **In the mock,** a scheme set up in Subsidy masters has no categories until its masters are entered, so the category preview answers 404 there. That is the mock's existing behaviour for an unfinished scheme.
- **Not yet checked on staging.**

#### Files changed

- `src/features/subsidy/api/subsidy.schemas.ts`:
  - config `inputs`, `spacing_labels`, `pipeline` and `cap_mode`;
  - the new request fields;
  - the extra blocks, the jantri add-ons and deductions, and nullable matrix ids;
  - `guidedCost` and `DEFAULT_SUBSIDY_SCHEME`.
- `src/features/subsidy/lib/calculator-draft.ts`: the scheme inputs in the draft, checked, and sent only when listed.
- `src/features/subsidy/components/calculator-inputs.tsx`: `SchemeInputsCard`.
- `src/features/subsidy/components/subsidy-calculator.tsx`: the card, its fields placed for refusals, the waiting message, and the scheme picker's default.
- `src/features/subsidy/components/calculator-results.tsx`, `src/features/subsidy/lib/subsidy-labels.ts`: the guided cost label, the add-ons and deductions, the extra summary rows, and the warning titles.
- `src/mocks/handlers/subsidy.ts`: inputs by scheme, their refusals, and AP drip.
- `Docs/Plan.md` (§9.1), `Docs/Tested-Features.md`, `Docs/screenshots/subsidy/ap-*`: records and screens.

#### Tests

- `src/features/subsidy/components/subsidy-scheme-inputs.test.tsx`:
  - a scheme asking for none sends none;
  - AP drip waits for its guided cost and fittings amount, then sends them, and a typo is marked;
  - RJ sends its spacing, filters and existing equipment, and a spacing not in the list is a mistake;
  - a sprinkler asks for its set size;
  - an AP result with null matrix ids and the state's GST reads;
  - the screen, end to end: an AP scheme picked (it sorts before GGRC), the portal's figures entered, the guided cost and "GST paid by the state" shown.
- `src/features/subsidy/lib/calculator-draft.test.ts`: fixtures updated for the new config fields.
- Walked through in the mock: desktop light and phone dark.

### Subsidy completion: the farmer's share, the dispatch date, the bells, Sprinkler steps

`feature` · `SUBS-006` `SUBS-002` `NOTIF-001` `SO-008` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-15--feature--SUBS-006--subsidy-completion.md)

#### Before

The backend added these, all additive (`subsidy-completion.md`):

1. A subsidised order's `payable` is the farmer's share: at most the total, less scheme benefits.
2. `dispatched_on` on a subsidy file: the first dispatch of a subsidised order naming its lead. Stage 7 takes it as the supply date when `supply` isn't sent.
3. Six bell kinds about a subsidy file (`resource.type: subsidy_application`).
4. Reopening a closed file.
5. Sprinkler areas between two table steps: the next step's quantities, a pro-rata unit cost, and an `area_between_steps` warning.

The frontend had none of these, except reopening (4), which PR #137 builds. The Sprinkler area was a list of the table's steps. The bell showed subsidy notices with the plain icon and no link.

#### Now

- **The farmer's share (§1):**
  - the order schema reads `payable`;
  - a subsidised order's Subsidy card says "Payable ₹…: the farmer's share";
  - the mock works it out as the backend does: never below 0 or above the total.
- **The dispatch date (§2):**
  - a subsidy file shows **Dispatched on** beside the Reg. No., or "Not yet";
  - recording stage 7 says under the supply date "Dispatched on 12 Oct 2026. Left empty, the supply date is taken from it.";
  - the form already sent only changed fields, so an untouched supply date isn't sent and the backend fills it.
- **The bells (§3):** `subsidy_returned`, `subsidy_query`, `subsidy_tr_failed`, `subsidy_closed`, `subsidy_cancelled` and `subsidy_reopened` each have an icon. `subsidy_application` records open `/subsidy/{id}` and are named "Subsidy file".
- **Sprinkler steps (§5):**
  - the area is typed, like the other systems, and checked against the table's range ("Between 0.4 and 5 Ha.");
  - an area between two steps is calculated, with the warning in the handover's words: "The area is between table steps. Quantities use the next step; the unit cost is in between.";
  - a scheme needing an exact step still answers `exact_area_match_required` on the area.
- **The mock:**
  - `dispatched_on` comes from the first un-voided dispatch of a subsidised order naming the lead, and one seeded file short of stage 7 has one;
  - stage 7 fills `supply` from it when the key isn't sent;
  - Sprinkler takes 0.4 to 5 Ha, with the warning between steps.
- Checked on a desktop in light mode and a phone in dark mode: the file's Dispatched on, stage 7's hint, and a 1.3 Ha Sprinkler. axe found nothing. The bell and the payable line are checked by tests.

#### Discussion

- **Not part of go-live** (the user, 13 Oct); plan item 18.
- **Stacked on #143** (#142, #141, #140 under it). Merge in order and retarget each to `integration` first.
- **Reopening a closed file (§4) is PR #137,** on its own branch.
- **The payable shows only on the Subsidy card.** The order page shows no payable or payments elsewhere yet: that is plan item 26 (payments).
- **Not yet checked on staging.**

### Reopen a closed subsidy file, and the document checklist

`feature` · `SUBS-015` `SUBS-007` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-15--feature--SUBS-015--reopen-a-closed-subsidy-file.md)

#### Before

A subsidy application closes by itself once every stage-16 amount has its stage-17 date. After that it takes no more entries. When a date or an amount had been entered wrong, nobody could correct it from the screen.

The backend added `POST /subsidy-applications/{id}/reopen` (`subsidy-completion.md` §4) and `GET /subsidy-document-types`, the checklist every application is given. The frontend used neither.

#### Now

- **Reopen** shows on a closed ("Fully paid") file, only for those with `subsidy.approve`: Admin Sales and the MD.
  - The closed file's note tells them they can reopen it to correct an entry, and that it closes again when the payment entries are complete.
  - The dialog asks why (1 to 500 characters) and says that the file's owner and the lead's owner are told.
  - Afterwards the file is open, with its stages and figures as they were, and **Record stage** and **Cancel** are back.
- **It closes again** only when an entry writes a stage-16 amount or a stage-17 date, as the backend checks.
- **Refusals:**
  - no reason: on the field;
  - `409 commission_settled`: "The dealer's commission is settled". The file stays closed;
  - `409 application_not_closed`: the dialog closes, a toast says why, and the file refreshes;
  - `403`: "Not yours to reopen".
- **Subsidy masters → Documents** lists the checklist from `GET /subsidy-document-types`.
  - Each item is numbered, with its code; an item no longer asked for is marked.
  - It is read only and the same for every scheme.
- **The mock:**
  - It seeds one closed file through every stage.
  - Reopen needs `subsidy.approve`.
  - A file closes again only on an entry that writes a payment field, so reopening and then opening the file no longer closes it.
  - It serves the checklist, and records `subsidy.reopened` on the lead's history.
- Checked on a desktop in light mode and a phone in dark mode: the closed file, the dialog, the reopened file and the checklist. axe found nothing.

#### Discussion

- **Why a Documents tab:** each application's checklist already names its items, so `GET /subsidy-document-types` adds nothing there. The tab lets an administrator read the list without opening an application. If the client wants the list editable, that needs a backend endpoint.
- **The commission rule can't be shown in the mock,** which has no dealer commissions; a test stands in for it.
- **Not yet checked on staging.**

#### Files changed

- `src/features/subsidy/api/subsidy-applications.schemas.ts`, `.api.ts`, `.queries.ts`, `.mutations.ts`: `reopenApplication`, `listDocumentTypes` and their query and mutation.
- `src/features/subsidy/components/application-actions.tsx`: the Reopen button and dialog.
- `src/features/subsidy/components/application-detail.tsx`: `subsidy.approve`, and the closed note's hint.
- `src/features/subsidy/components/document-checklist-panel.tsx`: new, the checklist.
- `src/features/subsidy/components/subsidy-masters.tsx`: the Documents tab.
- `src/mocks/handlers/subsidy-applications.ts`: the reopen and checklist routes, a closed seeded file, and closing only on a payment entry.
- `src/lib/data-ids/registry.ts`, `Docs/Data-IDs.md`: SUBS-015, and `GET /subsidy-document-types` under SUBS-007.
- `Docs/Plan.md` (§9.1), `Docs/Tested-Features.md`, `Docs/screenshots/subsidy/`: records and screens.

### One set of meeting minutes on its own page

`feature` · `TASK-007` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-15--feature--TASK-007--one-set-of-minutes-on-its-own-page.md)

#### Before

A task created from meeting minutes said "From meeting minutes" as plain text. The minutes themselves showed only on the lead's page, in a list. From My day, Team or All tasks there was no way to read the meeting a task came from without finding the lead first. The backend's `GET /minutes/{id}` (`tasks-and-planner-contract.md`) was registered under TASK-007 but unused.

#### Now

### The Accounts queue, and the order counts behind its badge

`feature` · `ACCT-001` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-14--feature--ACCT-001--the-accounts-queue-and-the-order-counts-behind-its-badge.md)

#### Before

"Accounts queue" sat in the menu marked "Soon". The backend finished it in BE-022 (`accounts-queue-order-names.md`):

- `waiting_on` on `GET /orders`, `/orders/stats` and `/orders/export`;
- `GET /orders/stats` itself.

Accounts found their orders only through the Approvals inbox.

The menu item also asked for an `accounts` permission. The backend has no such module: the Accounts role holds `payments` (RBAC.md §6.2). So on the real backend the item could never have appeared.

#### Now

- **The Accounts queue,** at `/accounts`.
  - **The list:** every submitted order whose next approval step is Accounts' payment check. Each row shows its number (linked to the order), the party and dealer, type, owner, when it was submitted, and its value.
  - **Deciding:** **Decide in Approvals** for those who decide.
  - **Above the list:** "1 order waits on Accounts' payment check", and **Download Excel** for the queue.
  - **States:** skeleton, "Nothing waits on Accounts" (saying when an order arrives), an error with a reference, a later page failing while the rows stay.
- **The sidebar badge** on Accounts queue: the waiting orders, from `GET /orders/stats`'s `waiting_on.account_manager`.
  - It is checked again each minute.
  - It refreshes whenever an order or an approval changes.
- **Who sees it:** whoever may view payments, which is Accounts and Admin. A field officer has no menu item, and the page refuses them (APP-006).
- **The permission module** is `payments`, as the backend names it.
  - The mock's Accounts role holds payments view, create, edit and approve, as RBAC.md says.
  - A payment's documents follow `payments.edit`, as the backend's do.
- Checked on a desktop in light mode and a phone in dark mode. axe found nothing.

#### Discussion

- **Built like the Dispatch queue,** as rows rather than a table. "Show more" and the list skeleton now live in `queue-parts.tsx`, shared by both queues.
- **Deciding stays in Approvals.** The queue sends each order there rather than repeating the decision dialog.
- **Recording a payment** ("What Accounts records" in the handover) needs the payments screens, plan item 26. The queue has no such button yet.
- **The badge reads the stats without `waiting_on`,** as the handover says. Its key sits under the order lists, so every write and approval decision that refreshes the lists refreshes it too.
- **Stacked on #125,** which reworked the same order list parameters and mock filter. Merge #125 first, then retarget this PR to `integration`.

### An empty conversation names its colleague after a reload

`feature` · `MSG-004` `MSG-002` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-14--feature--MSG-004--an-empty-conversation-names-its-colleague-after-a-reload.md)

#### Before

The backend lists a conversation only once someone writes in it, and had no way to read one on its own. So the thread named the colleague of a just-started conversation from the answer to "start", kept in the page's memory.

After a reload, or from a link a colleague shared, an empty conversation's header read "Conversation". The empty state said "No messages yet" rather than whom to write to, and the box had no name. The backend has since added `GET /conversations/{id}` (BE-021).

#### Now

- **The thread reads a conversation it can't find in the list** from `GET /conversations/{id}`. That covers a conversation just started, opened after a reload, or opened from a link.
  - The header names the colleague and their role.
  - The empty state reads "Say hello to Imran Sheikh".
  - The box is labelled "Message Imran Sheikh".
- **A listed conversation is not read again;** the list, which is polled, stays the source.
- **Starting a conversation** seeds that read with the backend's answer, so the header doesn't wait for it.
- **If the read fails,** the header says "Conversation", as before, and the thread still loads and sends. A conversation that isn't the user's is a 404, and the page shows not-found, as it already did from the messages call.
- The mock answers `GET /conversations/{id}`, including the 404.
- Checked on a desktop in light mode and a phone in dark mode: a new conversation with Imran Sheikh, one read of the conversation each time. axe found nothing.

#### Discussion

- **Under the list's key.** The read's query key sits under the conversation list's, so a refresh of the list (after a send, a start, or a colleague found to have left) refreshes it too.
- **Groups are not handled here.** The backend's `Conversation` now carries `kind` and `group`, with `participant` null for a group (FS-048). The frontend still expects one colleague, so a group in the list or behind a link would be a contract error. Groups are plan item 7, which widens the schema.
- **A reload can't be shown in the mock walk:** the mock's data resets on a reload, so a new conversation is gone. A unit test covers it: the conversation is started outside the page and the thread names it from the backend.

#### Files changed

- `src/features/messages/api/messages.api.ts`: `getConversation`.
- `src/features/messages/api/messages.queries.ts`: `conversationQueryOptions` and `messageKeys.conversation`. They replace the in-memory `startedConversationQueryOptions`.
- `src/features/messages/api/messages.mutations.ts`: starting a conversation seeds the read.
- `src/features/messages/components/conversation-thread.tsx`: reads an unlisted conversation.
- `src/mocks/handlers/messages.ts`: `GET /conversations/:conversationId`.
- `src/lib/data-ids/registry.ts`, `Docs/Data-IDs.md`: MSG-004 reads one conversation.
- `Docs/Plan.md` (§9.1), `Docs/Tested-Features.md`, `Docs/screenshots/messages-notifications/`: records and screens.

#### Tests

- `src/features/messages/api/messages.api.test.ts`, `[MSG-004]`:
  - one conversation read before anyone writes in it, and a listed one;
  - a 404 for one that isn't the user's.
- `src/features/messages/components/conversation-thread.test.tsx`, `[MSG-002] ConversationThread`:
  - the colleague named after a reload, from the backend, with the box labelled;
  - "Conversation" when the read fails, with the thread still there;
  - the existing test for a just-started conversation now seeds the read.
- Walked through in the mock: desktop light and phone dark.

### Dashboard: area by irrigation system, and orders against target

`feature` · `RPT-001` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-14--feature--RPT-001--dashboard-area-by-irrigation-system-and-orders-against-target.md)

#### Before

The backend's `GET /dashboard/overview` gained two fields with FS-052 (`dashboard.md`, "Five small changes" in `dealer-recruitment-and-small-changes.md`):

- `area_by_system`: open and won leads now, by irrigation system, with their land in hectares;
- `targets_by_month`: this month and the five before it, the order value target against what was sold, or `null` without a targets permission.

The dashboard read neither. The mock sent neither, and the frontend knew no `targets` permission.

#### Now

- **Area by irrigation system,** a new dashboard card.
  - One row per system, most land first: its name, "38.5 hectares" and "14 leads", over a bar of the land.
  - "No open or won leads yet." when there are none. "None of these leads has its land recorded yet." when every system's land is zero.
- **Orders against target,** a new dashboard card.
  - One row per month, oldest first; the current month is marked "so far".
  - Each row: a bar of what was sold, a line across it at the target, and "₹9.84 L of ₹12 L 82%" beside it.
  - A key names the bar (Sold) and the line (Target), so neither rests on colour.
  - A month without a target says "no target". A role that can't see sales orders (`achieved: null`) sees "Target ₹12 L" and a description to match.
  - "No targets set for the last six months." when there is nothing to draw.
- **Left out without a targets permission.** The backend sends `null` to Accounts, Dispatch, QA and partner users, and the card is not drawn. The area card then takes the row, its rows spread over columns.
- **An older backend** without either field reads as no areas and no targets card, not as a broken contract. A month that isn't `YYYY-MM` is a contract violation.
- **`ProportionBar` takes a `marker`:** a line at a value on the bar's own scale, with a ring in the card's colour where it crosses the fill. It has stories now.
- **`formatMonth`:** "2026-10" reads "Oct 2026", in India's time.
- **The `targets` permission module,** and the mock's grants as migration 035 seeds them: officers view their own, managers view and set their team's, Admin everything.
- Checked on a desktop in light mode and a phone in dark mode as a State Manager, as Accounts (no targets) and as a field officer in dark mode. axe found nothing.

#### Discussion

- **Rows, not a column chart.** Both cards follow the dashboard's existing pipeline and sources cards: a label, the figures in text, and a thin bar. Every value is printed beside its bar, so there is no hover tooltip to find and nothing is lost on a phone.
- **One hue.** The bars are the primary colour; the target line is the text colour with a ring. No status colour marks a month over or under target: the percentage says it.
- **One scale per card.** The targets bars share the largest of every target and sale, so months compare with each other, and a month over target runs past its line.
- **Sorted by land** rather than the backend's name order, so the comparison reads at a glance.
- **Not yet checked on staging.** PR #128.

#### Files changed

- `src/features/dashboard/api/dashboard.schemas.ts`: `area_by_system` and `targets_by_month`, read as `areaBySystem` (default `[]`) and `targetsByMonth` (default `null`); `amount`.
- `src/features/dashboard/components/dashboard-charts.tsx`: new, `AreaBySystemCard`, `TargetsCard` and their skeleton.
- `src/features/dashboard/components/dashboard-overview.tsx`: the new row, and its skeleton.
- `src/components/patterns/proportion-bar.tsx`, `proportion-bar.stories.tsx`: the `marker`; stories.
- `src/lib/format/date.ts`, `index.ts`: `formatMonth`.
- `src/lib/auth/permissions.ts`, `src/mocks/data/permissions.ts`: the `targets` module and its grants.
- `src/mocks/handlers/dashboard.ts`: both fields, with `null` targets for a role without them.
- `src/lib/data-ids/registry.ts`: RPT-001's title and note.
- `Docs/Plan.md` (§9.1), `Docs/Tested-Features.md`, `Docs/screenshots/dashboard/`: records and screens.

### Order list filters by area and office

`feature` · `SO-001` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-14--feature--SO-001--order-list-filters-by-area-and-office.md)

#### Before

The orders list filtered by status, type, "Only my orders" and a search. The backend had added `territory_id` (up to 20, a state selecting its districts and talukas) and `owner_org_unit_id` (an office and the offices under it) to `GET /orders`, `/orders/stats` and `/orders/export` ("Five small changes" in `dealer-recruitment-and-small-changes.md`). The lead list already had an Area filter, but the orders list had neither.

#### Now

- **Area** on the orders list.
  - **Picking:** states, districts or talukas, drilling down from the top, up to 20. Each area covers everything under it.
  - **The list:** the whole territory tree (`GET /lookups/territories?parent_id=`), with no counts. Orders have no "areas with orders" endpoint, and the lead list's counts would be of leads.
  - **The empty state** names the place: "Amreli has no talukas. Go back and choose Amreli itself."
- **Office**, for staff only (a dealer never sees it): one open office, by name.
  - A district office reads "Under Gujarat State".
  - Choosing an office covers the offices under it.
  - While the list loads, or if it fails, the pill says so.
- **Both filters:**
  - are kept in the URL (`area=`, `office=`), so a link to a filtered list works;
  - count in "Reset filters", which clears them;
  - go to **Download Excel** with the rest.
- The lead list's Area filter works as before, with its counts.
- Checked on a desktop in light mode and a phone in dark mode. axe found nothing with either popover open or with the list filtered.

#### Discussion

- **One Area pill, two sources.** `LeadAreaFilter` takes `source: "leads" | "territories"`.
  - Both read one query, `areaRowsQueryOptions`, which gives the same rows either way.
  - The territories rows have their own cache key, so they never mix with the territory picker's search results.
  - `searchTerritories` gained an optional `parentId`.
- **Office is a single choice,** because the backend takes one `owner_org_unit_id`. The open offices fit in one list of 50 (`GET /org-units?is_open=true`, readable by anyone signed in).
- **`GET /orders/stats` isn't used yet.** It comes with the Accounts queue, plan item 3, and will take the same filters.
- **Plan §9's paragraph** gets its sentence once #124, which merges the duplicated paragraph, is in. This PR updates only the §9.1 row, to stay clear of that merge.
- **The mock:**
  - the list and the export share one filter;
  - an order is in an area when its territory, or any above it, is chosen;
  - an office covers the offices under it;
  - the mock export now honours the filters too, as the backend does.

### No dialog close timer once the dialog has gone

`fix` · `APP-003` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-14--fix--APP-003--no-dialog-close-timer-once-the-dialog-has-gone.md)

#### Before

After a save, eleven dialogs show "Saved" and close themselves 600 ms later:

- leads: assign, stage, new lead;
- orders: every action;
- quotations;
- complaints;
- tasks: new, edit, action, minutes;
- approval limits.

Each cleared its timer when it went away, but none checked whether it had gone before starting one. `useAsyncAction` runs a success handler even after its component has unmounted, on purpose, so that the toast still shows. So a save that finished after the dialog was closed, or after the user left the page, started a timer that nothing would ever clear. It then closed a dialog that no longer existed.

In the browser this did nothing visible. In the unit tests, a timer could outlive its test file. On 13 October, CI on PR #124 failed after all 1010 tests had passed, with "ReferenceError: window is not defined" from the lead assign dialog's timer, firing after jsdom was torn down (`lead-assign.test.tsx`).

#### Now

- **One hook,** `useCloseAfterSuccess` in `src/hooks/`, closes a dialog a moment after a save:
  - its timer is cleared when the dialog goes;
  - it is never started once the dialog has gone.
- **Nine dialogs use it.** Their own copies are gone: three local hooks, the complaints' `useCloseLater`, and five inline timers.
- **The new-lead and new-task dialogs** also reset their form when they close. They keep their own timer, with the same never-after-it-has-gone guard.
- Nothing changes on screen.

#### Discussion

- **Why the timers and not `useAsyncAction`.** Not calling `onSuccess` after unmount would also stop the leak. But it would lose the toast, and the page change after a delete, when the user had closed the dialog mid-save. The timer is the only part that must not outlive the dialog.
- **Ported into PR #124,** whose CI it failed. The change is identical there, so it merges cleanly whichever lands first. Any other open PR picks it up from `integration`.

#### Files changed

- `src/hooks/use-close-after-success.ts`: new, the hook and `CLOSE_AFTER_SUCCESS_MS`.
- **Using the hook:**
  - `src/features/orders/components/order-dialog-shared.tsx`, `order-action-dialog.tsx`, `record-dispatch-form.tsx`;
  - `src/features/leads/components/lead-assign-dialog.tsx`, `lead-stage-dialog.tsx`;
  - `src/features/quotations/components/quotation-action-dialog.tsx`;
  - `src/features/complaints/components/complaint-dialog-parts.tsx`, `complaint-actions.tsx`, `complaint-targets.tsx`, `remedy-card.tsx`;
  - `src/features/tasks/components/edit-task-dialog.tsx`, `minutes-dialog.tsx`, `task-action-dialog.tsx`;
  - `src/features/approvals/components/approval-limit-dialog.tsx`.
- **Guarded in place:** `src/features/leads/components/new-lead-dialog.tsx`, `src/features/tasks/components/new-task-dialog.tsx`.

#### Tests

- `src/hooks/use-close-after-success.test.ts`, `[APP-003] useCloseAfterSuccess`:
  - closes after the moment;
  - forgets the close when the dialog goes first;
  - starts no timer when a save finishes after the dialog has gone (the case CI hit).
- The dialogs' own tests pass unchanged: leads, orders, quotations, complaints, tasks and approvals, 272 tests.

### The release's menu: only the screens a deployment releases

`feature` · `APP-007` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-13--feature--APP-007--the-release-s-menu-only-the-screens-a-deployment-releases.md)

#### Before

The client's box releases the go-live scope in two places:

- the backend grants only those modules' permissions (`backend/scripts/seed_prod.py`);
- the deploy script builds the frontend with `NEXT_PUBLIC_NAV_ONLY`, the go-live menu (`RELEASED_NAV` in `backend/scripts/deploy_staging.py`).

Nothing in the frontend read `NEXT_PUBLIC_NAV_ONLY`, so the menu followed permissions alone. Screens whose module was released for another reason still showed. QR codes rides on `leads`; Subsidy masters and Masters ride on `masters`, which is released for offices and territories.

#### Now

- **The variable.** `NEXT_PUBLIC_NAV_ONLY` (build time) is read and checked as a list of nav item ids, for example `dashboard,leads,quotations`. A badly formed value fails the build.
- **Outside the list,** a screen is gone from the sidebar and the command menu. Typing its address shows "You don't have access to this page", for every role, administrators included. Pages under a released item stay open, such as `/products/price-lists/…` under Products.
- **Inside the list,** permissions decide as before.
- **Unset or empty,** nothing changes: every screen the permissions allow shows. That covers local development, feature previews and the team's own staging box.

#### Discussion

- **One rule, in one place.** The list is checked in `canSeeNavItem`, which the sidebar, the command menu, the header and the route guard (APP-006) all use. Something left out of the menu can't be reached by address either.
- **Hiding is a courtesy.** The backend's permission rows are still what enforces the scope.
- **A test reads the deploy script.** It checks that every id in `RELEASED_NAV` exists in the menu, so a renamed nav item can't silently hide a released screen.
- **Widening the release** takes both changes: a new `RELEASED_NAV` and a frontend rebuild, plus the backend's `seed_prod.py --modules …` for the permissions.

#### Files changed

- `src/lib/env/client.ts` and its test: `NEXT_PUBLIC_NAV_ONLY` becomes `navOnly`.
- `src/components/layout/navigation.ts`: `isReleased`. `canSeeNavItem`, `visibleNavSections` and `canOpenPath` take the release list, defaulting to the build's.
- `src/components/layout/navigation.test.ts`: the release's tests.
- `.env.example`, `Docs/Environments.md`: the variable.
- `src/lib/data-ids/registry.ts`, `Docs/Data-IDs.md`: APP-007.
- `Docs/Tested-Features.md`: the story.

#### Tests

- **`src/components/layout/navigation.test.ts`, `[APP-007] the release's menu`:**
  - only released screens show for an administrator;
  - permissions still apply inside the release;
  - `/qr-codes` and `/subsidy-masters` are refused by address, while a page under a released item and a page outside the menu open;
  - no list releases everything;
  - every id the deploy script releases exists.
- **`src/lib/env/client.test.ts`:** the list is parsed, empty means everything, and a malformed list is refused.

### Channel partners: list, add, correct, close and import

`feature` · `CHNL-001` `CHNL-002` `CHNL-003` `CHNL-004` `CHNL-005` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-13--feature--CHNL-001--channel-partners-list-add-correct-close-and-import.md)

#### Before

"Channel partners" in the menu said "Soon". The backend serves the partner admin (`backend/docs/api/partners.md`) and the partner Excel import (`imports.md`, `kind=partners`) on `integration`. Without a screen, the client had no way to add a distributor, or a dealer or sub-dealer under one, before quoting through them.

#### Now

- **Channel partners** (`/partners`) is live for staff who read partners.
  - The list is newest first, with a total. Each row shows the type, code, the partner above, territory, contact and active users.
  - Search by name, code or contact person. Filter by type and by Open, Closed, or both (open by default). A partner's page links to the partners under it, which arrive as an "Under …" filter chip.
  - **Download Excel** exports the filtered list. **Show more** pages on, and keeps the rows already shown if the next page fails.
- **A partner's page** has four cards:
  - Where it sits: its type and price tier, the partner above it (linked), its territory, and a link to those under it.
  - Business: GSTIN, PAN, GST registration, active users, and when it was added.
  - Contact.
  - Credit terms, shown to staff only.
  - Actions: **Edit**; **Close** or **Reopen**; **Add a dealer** (or **Add a sub-dealer**) under it. A closed partner says what closing means.
- **New partner** (CHNL-002).
  - Choose Distributor, Dealer or Sub-dealer first. A dealer then asks for its distributor, and a sub-dealer for its dealer, from the open partners of that type.
  - Then the territory, code, business name, GSTIN, PAN, GST registration, contact details and credit terms.
  - The form names what is missing or misshapen before sending. A refusal returns to its field, such as "Already in use." for a used code.
  - Opened from a partner's page, the form starts as the next type down under that partner, in that partner's territory.
- **Edit** (CHNL-003) sends only what changed and says "Nothing changed yet" until something does. A cleared optional field is sent as null. The code, the type and the parent are shown but fixed, and only staff see the territory and credit terms.
- **Close** (CHNL-004) says how many users will be signed out and deactivated. **Reopen** says the partner's users stay deactivated until each is reactivated in Users & roles.
- **Import from Excel** (CHNL-005) reuses the import dialog from MSTR-007.
  - A dealer names its distributor's code, which may be a row in the same file.
  - The review shows each bad row's reason as the backend words it. The preview shows the territory the backend worked out from the state and district.
  - **Import good rows only** adds the rest, parents first.
- **Who sees it.** Admin-Sales and the MD do everything. District and State Managers add, edit, close and reopen partners in their area (`partners.edit`). Field officers and Regional Managers read only. Partner users get no menu item, and the page is closed to them (APP-006).
- Checked on a phone in dark mode and on a desktop in light mode. axe found nothing.

#### Discussion

- **Staff only for now.** The backend also lets a distributor or dealer add the next type down under itself from the portal, with no credit terms. That needs a portal menu item and the partner's own id as the parent. Both wait on the client's word: `TODO(CHNL-002)` sits on the nav item, and the question is in the pull request.
- **Credit terms are recorded, not enforced.** The contract says so (H12), and the form's help text says so too.
- **Closing is staff only.** It needs `partners.edit`, and the backend refuses a partner user even with it.
- **Mock changes.**
  - The mock's partners live in `mockDb.partners`, seeded from the shared `MOCK_PARTNERS`, so leads, orders and users still point at the same ids.
  - `/lookups/partners` now reads the same table, so a partner added here can be picked on a lead.
  - District and State Managers gain `partners.create` and `edit` in the mock, as in RBAC.md §6.1. Regional Managers keep view.
- **Import mock.** The mock's partner fields are now the backend's, `GST registered` included. Its row rules follow `domain/imports/rows.py` (`parse_partners`, `finish_partners`): type words, state by name or code, district in that state, codes in use, repeated codes, and parents in the file or already added.

### Documents on leads, quotations, orders and dispatches

`feature` · `DOC-001` `DOC-002` `DOC-003` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-13--feature--DOC-001--documents-on-leads-quotations-orders-and-dispatches.md)

#### Before

The client handles purchase orders, payment slips, invoices and transport receipts outside the app. The backend now keeps them on the record they belong to (FS-050, `backend/docs/api/documents.md`, handover `documents-and-replacement-chain.md`). The frontend had no screen for it, so a bill or PO PDF could not be attached anywhere.

#### Now

- **A Documents card** on the lead, quotation and order pages, and a Documents section on each dispatch on the order page.
  - The list is newest first. Each row shows the document's name (or its type), the type, the file name and size, and who added it and when.
  - **Open** uses the backend's ten-minute link, which is renewed before it runs out and is never fetched with the bearer token. A HEIC photo, which browsers can't show, is offered as **Download** instead.
- **On the lead**, the card shows everything on the lead and on what came from it: its quotations, their orders, those orders' dispatches, and leads merged into it. Each row names its record, such as "Quotation QT/GJ/…" or "Order SO/GJ/…", linked where the record has a page.
- **Attach a file** (DOC-002).
  - **The form.** Pick what it is from the backend's types, then give a name for "Other" (a note otherwise, up to 80 characters), then choose one file.
  - **Checks before sending.** A missing type or file, a missing name for "Other", a file over 10 MB, and a file that isn't JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC or PDF are each named first.
  - **Refusals.** Each backend refusal has its sentence: 413; `attachment_type`; `too_many_documents` at 50; `record_closed` on a merged lead or a voided dispatch; `storage_unavailable`; 403; 404.
  - **The same file again.** It answers with the one already there, and the toast says so.
- **Remove** (DOC-003) asks first. It's offered to whoever added the document, and to staff who may add to the record it sits on (on a lead, the lead's own documents).
- **Who adds**, from the handover:
  - Leads: whoever edits them, a dealer on their own leads.
  - Quotations: staff who edit quotations.
  - Orders: whoever edits them.
  - Dispatches: Dispatch, or the order's editor.
  - A merged lead and a voided dispatch take none.
- Checked on a phone in dark mode and a desktop in light mode. axe found nothing.

#### Discussion

- **One component, two shapes.** It's a card on a page. On the order page each dispatch gets a section, named after its number ("Documents on D/SO/…") so the lists and buttons on that page stay distinct.
- **Links are fetched one per document and renewed every nine minutes**, as the complaint and subsidy files do. A list holds 50 documents at most.
- **The type picker shows every type the backend lists.** That includes the five a dealer application uses (GST certificate, PAN card…). BE-025 asks for a `record_type` filter rather than the frontend hard-coding which types to hide.
- **Payments aren't built here.** The backend takes documents on payments (Accounts). There is no payments screen yet, so none is offered.
- **Stacked on #111** for its upload plumbing: the multipart reader in the mock, multipart in jsdom tests, and `formatFileSize`.

- `../docs/Backend-Tasks.md` — BE-025.

### Excel import with column matching, and price lists by sale type

`feature` · `MSTR-007` `MSTR-008` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-13--feature--MSTR-007--excel-import-with-column-matching-and-price-lists-by-sale.md)

#### Before

The backend's Excel import (FS-062, `backend/docs/api/imports.md`) and price lists by sale type (FS-061) had reached `integration` with no screens. A draft price list's rates were typed in one by one. A quotation's or order's items were added row by row. A price list had no sale type, and the builders priced every line from the general list whatever the quotation's sale type.

#### Now

- **One import dialog for every kind (MSTR-007).** Four steps, shown as a trail: **Upload** (`.xlsx` or `.csv`, up to 10 MB, checked before it is sent), **Match columns**, **Review**, **Done**.
  - Match: every column in the file is listed with its five sample values and a picker. The pick is "Skip this column" or one of the import's fields, with "(required)" marked and each field's help line. The backend's suggested match is filled in. "Still to match: Rate" names what is missing. A workbook's sheet is picked from a list, and the row that holds the column names can be changed and read again. Both are a new upload of the same file.
  - Review: "N ready" and "N with errors" badges. A table of the bad rows gives row number, column and reason. The first 20 good rows show as they will be saved. Column warnings come from the backend.
  - Two ways out: **Import good rows only**, or **Import N rates**, which is all or nothing. Going **Back to matching** keeps the upload.
  - A rejected mapping is shown on its field. If rows changed since the check, the commit refusal names them. A published list, a finished import, a file too big or unreadable, and no permission each get one plain sentence. An upload closed without committing is discarded.
  - Keyboard: the long tables scroll inside regions that take focus.
- **Rates into a draft price list.** **Import from Excel** on a draft's sheet. Pick **Replace** (the file becomes the whole list) or **Merge** (rates not in the file stay). Done says "3 rates written, 2 skipped." and the sheet reloads. The button is off while typed rates are unsaved, so an import never lands on top of unsaved edits.
- **Items into a quotation or order.** **Import from Excel** on the Items card checks the file's lines and adds the good ones with "Add to quotation: the 2 good items" (or "to order"). Each added line takes its product, quantity and up to three discounts, then prices live like any other line. An untouched empty row gives way to the imported lines.
- **Price lists by sale type (MSTR-008).**
  - A list is for one sale type (Commercial, Industrial or Subsidy) or for all.
  - The new-list form asks for it. The list row and the sheet header show it.
  - A **Sale type** filter on Price lists has an "All sale types (general)" choice.
  - A copy keeps the sale type.
  - The quotation builder sends the quotation's sale type with every price preview. The order builder sends its order type the same way. A Subsidy quotation is priced from the Subsidy list where one is in force.
- Phone and desktop, light and dark. On a phone the dialog takes the screen's width and scrolls. Every step has its loading state on the button that started it.

#### Discussion

- **One dialog, three imports.** The backend serves partners, price-list rates and lines from one set of endpoints. The dialog takes the kind and a noun ("rates", "partners", "items"), so partners (CHNL, next pull request) reuse it unchanged.
- **Lines have no commit.** As the contract says, a `lines` import ends at the check. The good rows go into the builder's form and are saved with the quotation or order, so nothing is written until the person saves.
- **Multipart in tests.** jsdom's `fetch` can't send a `FormData` body to MSW, so `src/test/multipart-fetch.ts` encodes it in tests only. The mock reads multipart itself (`readMultipart`).
- **The mock reads CSV only.** It has no Excel reader, so any `.xlsx` gets a sample workbook for its kind, with a second sheet so the sheet picker shows. The backend reads both.
- **The review shows what the backend worked out.**
  - The backend's preview values for rates and lines are the product it found (`product`, `product_id`), not the item code or description typed. For partners, the preview gives the `territory` built from the state and district.
  - The review table therefore adds these values after the matched columns, and leaves out ids.
  - The mock now previews and words its reasons as the backend does (`domain/imports/rows.py`), for example "no product with item code PL-9999".
- **Imported lines name no unit.** The `lines` check returns the product but not its unit, so the quantity box takes its unit from the price preview once it arrives.
- **Fixed on the way:** "Indicative rate" on a priced line sat in a `<dl>` without a term (axe `definition-list`). It now has a visually hidden "Rate status" term.
- **A flaky smoke test, fixed on the way.** The sign-in page fades in, and on a slow CI runner axe once measured the Sign in button at 97% opacity: 4.34:1 instead of the token's 4.58:1. The axe helper in `e2e/smoke.spec.ts` now waits for entrance animations to finish (endless ones, such as spinners, are left running).
- **Not checked on staging yet.** The import endpoints are on `integration` (backend). The 🔌 check is in the PR's test plan.

#### Files changed

- `src/features/imports/` — new: the contract (`imports.schemas.ts`), calls (`imports.api.ts`), mutations, refusal messages (`lib/import-refusals.ts`), the four-step `ImportDialog`, and API tests.
- `src/features/products/api/` — `sales_type` on price lists, the list filter, and the copy keeps it.
- `src/features/products/components/price-lists-panel.tsx` — the Sale type filter, the form field, and the row label.
- `src/features/products/components/price-list-sheet.tsx` — sale type in the header; **Import from Excel** on a draft.

### Amend an approved order

`feature` · `SO-007` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-13--feature--SO-007--amend-an-approved-order.md)

#### Before

Once an order was approved, nothing on it could change. The only way out was to cancel it and type a new one, which lost its number and its history. The backend has served `POST /orders/{id}/amend` since FS-036 (`settings-amend-reopen-contract.md`, migration 041), with "Amend after a voided dispatch" added in migration 064. The frontend had no screen for it.

#### Now

- **Amend order…** sits in an approved order's More menu, next to Cancel.
  - **Who sees it:** staff who edit orders, or who own the order.
  - **When:** while nothing has shipped.
  - **Never offered:** to partner users, on a replacement order, or once something has shipped.
- **The dialog.** It asks what needs to change, and why. The reason is required, and is kept on the order and its history. It explains what follows:
  - the order goes back to draft under the same number;
  - it needs approval again;
  - its PDF is withdrawn until then;
  - any payment instalments are cleared for Accounts to set again.
- **The amended draft** shows a banner: "Amended after approval · it was approved at ₹…".
  - It counts the amends when there were several.
  - It shows the reason, for staff; a partner user reads none.
  - It says what to do next; while the order waits again, it says that too.
- **The old approval chain** stays visible as "Approval before the amend", saying it starts again from the first step on submit.
- **The history** reads "Amended: back to draft" with the approved total. The lead's history reads "Sales order amended, back to draft".
- **The edit screen** fixes the order type of an amended order, and says why. A refused change (`422 order_type_fixed`) has its own sentence.
- **Refusals, each in words:**
  - `409 voided_dispatch_holds_lines`: "This order had a dispatch voided. Cancel it and create a new one.", as the backend's handover asks;
  - `409 order_has_payments`;
  - `422 order_type_fixed`;
  - `409 order_dispatched`;
  - `409 status_changed`, which closes the dialog and shows the latest.
- Checked on a desktop in light mode and a phone in dark mode. axe found nothing on the dialog, the amended order or the edit screen.

#### Discussion

- **In the More menu, beside Cancel,** as the contract's "Screens" section puts it. It is rare, and it undoes an approval, so it doesn't sit with the everyday buttons.
- **What the screen checks first:** staff only (the backend refuses portal roles, GAP-352), the order approved, nothing shipped, not a replacement.
- **What only the backend knows:** whether money is allocated, or a voided dispatch still names the lines. The order carries neither, so the backend's refusal says it in words.
- **The old chain on a draft.** `GET /orders/{id}` returns the order's latest approval request. After an amend that is the chain that approved it before, so a draft showed four green steps. Retitling it keeps the record without suggesting the draft is approved.
- **The setting `order_amend_reapproval`** (`always` or `value_rises`) decides whether a total that didn't rise goes straight to Accounts on resubmit. The screen doesn't read it. The wording says "needs approval again", which holds either way. The settings screen is plan item 21.
- **Plan records:** `Docs/Plan.md` had two copies of the §9 paragraph after #114. They are merged into one, so partners and documents both appear once.

#### Files changed

- `src/features/orders/api/orders.schemas.ts`: `amend_count`, `amended_from_total`, `amend_reason` on the order (defaulted, so older responses still parse).
- `src/features/orders/api/orders.api.ts`, `orders.mutations.ts`: `amendOrder`, `useAmendOrder`.
- `src/features/orders/lib/order-lifecycle.ts`: the `amend` action, `isStaff` in the permissions, four refusals, the `order.amended` history line.
- `src/features/orders/hooks/use-order-actions.ts`: passes `isStaff`.
- `src/features/orders/components/order-actions.tsx`, `order-action-dialog.tsx`: the menu item and the dialog.

- `src/features/orders/components/order-approval.tsx`: "Approval before the amend".

- `src/features/leads/lib/timeline-entries.ts`: the lead's history line.

### CI green again: CHANGELOG.md regenerated, and two tests that depended on timing

`fix` · `REPO-001` `QUOT-007` `TASK-005` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-13--fix--REPO-001--ci-green-again-changelog-md-regenerated-and-the-approval.md)

#### Before

GitHub Actions runs again, and two checks failed on `integration` after #111 and #114:

- **"CHANGELOG.md is up to date".** The stacked PRs #112 and #113 merged into the MSTR-007 branch, and that branch then merged into `integration` (#114). The generated `CHANGELOG.md` was never rebuilt after the last merge, so `npm run changelog:build -- --check` found it stale.
- **`[QUOT-007] Ask for approval`** timed out on CI looking for "Waiting for approval". The CI output shows why: the page was still inert behind the closing dialog, and an inert page is hidden from role queries. A slow runner outlasted `findByRole`'s default second. It passes locally.
- **`[TASK-005]` refuses an officer cancelling a task someone else gave them** failed locally on 13 October. It searched the seed for an open task of the user's given by someone else. The seed settles tasks whose due time has passed, so by late morning that task was done and the search found nothing. The result depended on the hour.

#### Now

- `CHANGELOG.md` is rebuilt from the entries, so the check passes.
- The approval test first waits for the dialog to close, then finds the button, each with a 5-second ceiling. It still fails at once if the button never appears or isn't disabled.
- The task test makes its own precondition: it takes an open task of the user's and gives it a manager as the one who assigned it, then expects the 403. `afterEach` resets the mock database.

#### Discussion

- Nothing on screen changes; the client's app is the same.
- `npm run verify` runs `changelog:check` but not `changelog:build -- --check`, so a stale `CHANGELOG.md` only shows up on CI. Run `npm run changelog:build` after every merge into a branch, as `Docs/Frontend-Handover.md` §4.13 says.

#### Files changed

- `CHANGELOG.md`: regenerated.
- `src/features/quotations/components/quotation-actions.test.tsx`: the `[QUOT-007]` test waits for the dialog to close.
- `src/features/tasks/api/tasks.test.ts`: the `[TASK-005]` test sets up its own task.

#### Tests

- `npx vitest run --project unit src/features/quotations/components/quotation-actions.test.tsx`: 7 passed, three runs in a row.
- `npx vitest run --project unit src/features/tasks/api/tasks.test.ts`: 27 passed, at the hour it had failed.
- `npm run changelog:build -- --check` passes.
- `npm run verify` passes.

## 12 October 2026

### A frontend handover: the build process, step by step, and everything left

`docs` · `REPO-001` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-12--docs--REPO-001--a-frontend-handover-the-build-process-step-by-step-and.md)

#### Before

The way the frontend was built lived only in one long working session:

- how a feature goes from a backend handover to a merged PR;
- the browser walks, screenshots and axe checks;
- how PRs are split and stacked;
- the traps already hit.

`AGENTS.md` holds the rules but not the working loop. `Docs/Plan.md` and `docs/PendingFeatures.md` list what is left, but the second dates from 3 October. A new developer or AI session would have had to rediscover all of it.

#### Now

`Docs/Frontend-Handover.md`, linked from the "Read these first" table in `AGENTS.md`, covers:

- **§0–3:**
  - where to start;
  - the project in one page;
  - the user's standing rules for replies, code, security and commits;
  - the toolchain: commands, the mock dev server, Chromium, and CI blocked by billing.
- **§4: the loop every feature followed:**
  - pick and read the contract;
  - branch;
  - Data IDs;
  - permissions;
  - the API layer;
  - a mock with the backend's rules;
  - the UI patterns;
  - the browser walk, including the Playwright and axe helper to paste (the sign-in comes from environment variables);
  - API and UI tests;
  - the records (changelog, Plan §9, Tested-Features, Backend-Tasks, screenshots);
  - the final checks;
  - commit, push and PR;
  - resolving conflicts by merging `integration`.
- **§5–8:**
  - how work was split into PRs and stacked (the subsidy stack as the example);
  - why no subagents were used;
  - a map of the codebase;
  - the traps already hit.
- **§9:** what is built, by area, with its PRs.
- **§10: everything left, in order:**
  - **P0:** the go-live fixes for leads, quotations and orders from the 10 Oct walk.
  - **P1:** backend pick-ups: BE-021, BE-022 with payments, BE-023 and BE-024 when ticked, subsidised orders, subsidy completion.
  - **P2:** 22 modules the backend serves with no screens, each with its handover file, plus the dealer-portal walk.
  - **The measured gap:** every endpoint in `backend/docs/api` (372) compared with every endpoint the frontend's mock serves (178). That is a built/total table per module, the missing pieces of modules otherwise built (orders amend and subsidy, subsidised quotations, group chats, lookups admin, reopen actions…), and new fields on built screens (dashboard charts, order filters, land in hectares).
- **§12:** all 194 endpoints without a frontend, and the script to measure the gap again.
- **§11:** a first message for the next session.

#### Discussion

- **One file, in `Docs/`, beside the other records.** The next session reads `AGENTS.md` first, so the link there is how it finds the handover.
- **No credentials in it.** The walk helper reads the demo sign-in from environment variables, and points to `Docs/Tested-Features.md` for the mock fixture. Real staging logins come from the user.
- **The P0 items summarise the backend's walk-fix handovers.** The file says to read those first, since they are the source.
- **The gap was measured, not guessed.** The first draft listed whole modules by their handover names and missed the half-built ones. The comparison against the mock catches every unused endpoint; the field-level changes come from reading the recent handovers.
- **Status is pinned to `integration` at `ed010e1`** (11 October 2026). The file says to check `git log` and `docs/Backend-Tasks.md` for anything newer.

#### Files changed

- `Docs/Frontend-Handover.md`: new.
- `AGENTS.md`: a "Continue the build" row in "Read these first".

#### Tests

None: documentation only. Checked by hand:

- every file and folder the handover names exists, including `backend/docs/architecture/RBAC.md`, the handover files and the API docs;
- the commands match `package.json`;
- the open asks match `docs/Backend-Tasks.md`;
- the open PRs match GitHub on 11 October.

### Go-live fixes from the 10 Oct staging walk

`fix` · `APP-006` `APP-003` `LEAD-003` `LEAD-005` `LEAD-008` `LEAD-013` `LEAD-014` `APPR-001` `APPR-002` `QUOT-002` `SO-002` `CMPL-003` `AUTH-001` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-12--fix--APP-006--go-live-fixes-from-the-10-oct-walk.md)

#### Before

The 10 Oct staging walk of leads, quotations and orders (handovers `walk-fixes-10-oct.md` and `walk-fixes-10-oct-whatsapp-history-approvals.md`, "Yours (frontend)") found these on the frontend. The backend side of each was already done.

- **F-1:** a dealer saw the lead score, the duplicates box and the "Possible duplicates" button.
- **F-8:** a dealer could open `/approval-limits`, `/qr-codes` and `/dispatch` by typing the address. The empty approval limits said "Ask the backend team to seed them".
- **F-9:** the channel-partner box held "No channel partner" as text, so typing searched `q=No channel partnerBhavesh`.
- **F-11:** a step nobody of its role could decide still read "Waiting now" on an order's or refund's trail, and "Waiting for a District Manager…" on a quotation.
- **F-13:** the first click on a page that had just opened was lost on `/tasks`, `/leads`, the lead page and `/approvals`; the next Approve after a decision took several clicks.
- **F-14:** "Preparing the PDF" stayed after Send until a reload when the tab was in the background.
- **F-16:** the timeline said "merged another lead", "Asha Patel flagged 6 possible duplicates", "Quotation discount approved Draft", "the customer · Quotation opened by the customer", and gave a discount decision two lines.
- **F-17:** access-denied pages showed "REF TASK-001 · <uuid>" under the page's own header and filters.
- **F-19:** "by SMS" on the dealer sign-in; the QR code's internal label and "Loading…" on the farmer's enquiry form; an em dash on QR codes; "Your territory at a glance" for the admin and MD; quotation-only copy on orders typed in directly; "10.00 defective of 100.00 NOS"; no confirmation before a complaint submit, which messages the contact; the Reason box red as soon as its list opened.
- **Changed responses:** the score is now a whole number sent as `"28.00"`; an assign that changes the partner re-prices the lead's drafts; leads take land in hectares (FS-052).

#### Now

- **Route guards (APP-006, F-8).** A page whose menu item the user can't see can't be opened by its address either: the shell shows "You don't have access to this page" with **Back to the dashboard**, and the top bar says "Polysil CRM" instead of the page's title. The page itself, its header, filters and skeleton are never drawn. One rule, the nav's, covers every page; `/leads/duplicates` is staff only too. Approval limits is now a staff-only menu item, as its endpoint is.
- **No reference on a 403 (F-17).** Nothing failed, so `ErrorState` shows no "Ref" for a 403 anywhere.
- **Dealers (F-1, F-8).** No score, no possible-duplicates notice and no "Possible duplicates" button for a partner user. On QR codes, New QR code, Edit and Switch off are staff only, even if the page is opened.
- **Approval limits, empty:** "No approval limits are set." and why it matters, nothing more.
- **Channel partner box (F-9).** "No channel partner" (and "Unassigned" for the owner) is the placeholder; typing starts a fresh search. Choosing nobody empties the box.
- **Stalled steps (F-11).** The step waiting now reads "No District Manager to decide. With the next manager up." on an order's trail, a complaint refund's trail and a quotation's discount notice.
- **First click (F-13).** Only the page being left animates now: it slides and fades out over the new page, which takes clicks at once. The approval decision dialog closes as soon as the decision is saved (the toast confirms it), so the next row takes the next click.
- **PDF (F-14).** The quotation, order and customer-link pages keep checking while the tab is in the background.
- **Timeline (F-16).**
  - "Asha Patel merged POL/GJ/2026-27/00094 into this lead", each number a link.
  - "6 possible duplicates found: 00083, 00088, …", with no person's name: the system found them.
  - "Asha Patel marked 00083 as not a duplicate."
  - "The customer opened QT/…", on the lead and as "Opened by the customer" alone on the quotation.
  - A draft is "draft quotation v1" or "draft order".
  - A discount decision is one line, on the lead and on the quotation's history.
- **Copy (F-19).** "a 6-digit code is on its way on WhatsApp"; no QR label and no "Loading…" before a state on the enquiry form; no em dash on QR codes; the dashboard reads "Leads, quotations, orders and service at a glance."; delivery, delete and cancel dialogs on a direct order don't mention quotations; "10 defective of 100 NOS".
- **Complaint submit (F-19, F-3).** Submit asks first: "Submit for the manager's check?", naming the contact and their mobile, who "gets a WhatsApp at each step, once messages are switched on". A refusal stays in the dialog. The form's hint says the same.
- **Reason box (F-19).** A list field no longer turns red when its list opens; only when it is closed or left without a choice, or on submit. This is the shared `LookupSelect`, so the lost reason and every other admin list behave the same.
- **Leads.** The score is a whole number. A partner change refreshes the quotations, so a draft shows its new prices. The New lead and Edit forms ask for land in hectares and send `land_hectares`; the lead page shows "1.8 hectares (4.45 acres)".
- **Theme (F-20).** Checked by eye: with the computer in dark mode, choosing Light gives a light page.
- **Checked** on a phone in dark mode and a desktop in light mode, as a dealer and as staff. axe found nothing.

#### Discussion

- **F-13's cause.** Reproduced in Chromium: going to Tasks from the menu and clicking New task as soon as it showed sent the click to `<main>` every time. The arriving page was captured into the view transition, and Chrome doesn't hit-test a captured element until the transition ends (about 350 to 500 ms). `::view-transition { pointer-events: none }` was already set, and doesn't help with this. Animating only the leaving page keeps the direction cue and never captures the page people are about to use. The rejected option was skipping the transition on pointer-down: the click is already aimed at `<main>` by then. The e2e test `[APP-003] Page transitions` fails on the old code and passes now.
- **The approvals clicks.** In the mock the next row responded once the dialog had gone; the lost clicks landed on the dialog's overlay during the 600 ms it stayed open to show its tick, while the list behind already showed the next row. On staging the wait is longer. The inbox is used many times a day, so the dialog now closes at once.
- **`/qr-codes` for a dealer.** The walk asks for a route guard; the backend note describes a read-only dealer view. The page isn't in a dealer's menu, so the guard applies, and the page also hides its writes from partners. **Open question for the user:** should dealers get QR codes in their menu, read-only?
- **F-19, menus.** A field officer's Assign, QR codes, Dispatch queue and Complaint targets all follow from the role table (RBAC.md §6.1: `leads` V:own CE, `dispatch` V:own, `complaints` V:own CE; the backend lets a field officer set the partner, not the owner, and the dialog says so). Nothing changed; **open question for the user** whether the client wants them out of the menu.
- **F-19, the sixth digit.** The enquiry form and the dealer sign-in already submit on the sixth digit; unchanged.
- **F-12** (no files on a complaint after the QC verdict) is the backend's rule; **open question for the user** to confirm with the client. Nothing changed.
- **Not done here:** a "Deleted leads" view (`deleted=true`, optional in the handover), and the mock's quotation pricing for products added in Products & prices (mock-only polish). Both stay in the handover's §10.
- **Land.** The backend stores hectares and returns acres beside them (FS-052). A lead with only acres keeps them: the edit form sends land only when it changes.
- **`EmptyState` and `EmptyTitle` take a `level`** (2 or 3, default 3), as `CardTitle` does, so a page-sized empty state (access denied, not found) sits under the top bar's h1 without skipping a level.

## 11 October 2026

### Products and prices: the catalogue, GST by HSN code, and price lists

`feature` · `MSTR-004` `MSTR-005` `MSTR-006` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-11--feature--MSTR-004--products-and-prices-the-catalogue-gst-by-hsn-code-and-price.md)

#### Before

The web app could only pick products inside a quotation (MSTR-003). Nothing let the client add a product, give it an HSN code and a GST slab, or set its price. The backend serves all of it (`backend/docs/api/products.md`, `pricing.md`, handover `products-and-pricing.md`). Without these screens a client going live on leads, quotations and orders could not put its own catalogue in.

#### Now

**Admin → Products & prices** (`/products`) has three tabs, and the open tab is kept in the URL. Everyone on staff can read it. Admin-Sales and the MD can change it: they hold `products.edit` (the catalogue and tax) and `pricing.edit` (the price lists). Partners don't see it.

- **Products** (MSTR-004)
  - **The list.** A page of 50, with the total. Each row shows:
    - description and item code;
    - category, quotation block and unit;
    - HSN and GST slab, and MRP;
    - "No HSN", "2 stand-ins" and "Switched off" chips where they apply.
  - **Search and filters.** Search by description or item code. Filter by category, block and status (active by default, switched off, or all). Filters and page are kept in the URL.
  - **New product.**
    - Description. No two products may share one: "Another product already has this description."
    - Category and unit.
    - Quotation block (head unit, field, or either).
    - Optional item code, MRP and pack multiple, and "Eligible for subsidy".
    - What's missing is named before anything is sent.
  - **Opening a product** shows the same form.
    - Only what changed is sent. "Nothing changed yet" shows until something does.
    - A figure the backend still holds as a stand-in has a "Stand-in" chip, and setting it makes it the client's own.
    - **Switch off / Switch on.**
    - Read-only for anyone without `products.edit`.
- **Tax** (MSTR-005)
  - **On each product:**
    - the heading in force and its slab, or "No HSN code yet: quotations can't tax it";
    - its history, once it has changed;
    - a new HSN code from a date. The day the current heading started is refused, with what to do.
  - **The Tax rates tab:**
    - the rates in force today, or all of them, with "Starts later" and "Ended";
    - find a code by HSN;
    - **Set a rate**: HSN, a slab from the Council's list (0, 0.25, 3, 5, 12, 18, 28) and a start date, for every product under the code. **Change** opens it for that code.
- **Price lists** (MSTR-006)
  - **The list:** all, drafts or published. Each shows:
    - its phase: Draft, "Published, starts later", In force or Ended;
    - its scope: a state and a tier, or every one;
    - its dates;
    - how many rates it holds, and how many active products have none.
  - **New price list:** name, start date, an optional state and tier, and where the rates come from. It opens the new draft.
  - **The rate sheet** (`/products/price-lists/{id}`) has search and "Without a rate only".
    - On a draft, rates are typed in place and kept across pages and searches, with "2 unsaved changes" and **Discard**.
    - A rate with more than two decimals, or of 0, is named on its row, and **Save rates** stays off until it is fixed.
  - **Publish** needs saved rates. A list missing some asks you to tick "Publish without rates for N active products".
  - **A published list is read-only.** Its page says why. It can be **closed from a date** (its last day, forward only). It is corrected with **New list from this one**, which copies its scope and every rate into a new draft.
- **States:**
  - a skeleton for every list and the rate sheet;
  - empty, filtered-empty and past-the-end states;
  - a 404 for a list that doesn't exist;
  - refusals in words: 403, the 409s the backend names, and 422s on their fields.
- **Checked** on a phone in dark mode and on a desktop in light mode. axe found nothing.

#### Discussion

- **Categories and units come from the catalogue itself,** read from every page of `GET /products`, active products and switched-off ones. `POST /products` takes only known codes, but nothing lists them. A free-text box would turn a typo into a refusal. Asked of the backend as **BE-024** (`GET /lookups/product-categories`, `/lookups/uoms`). Until then, a category no product uses yet can't be chosen.
- **Saving rates reads the list's own rates first.** `PUT /price-lists/{id}/items` replaces them all, so the screen lays the edits over them: a typed rate is set, a cleared one removed, the rest kept. This means a sheet bigger than one page is never cut down to the page on screen.
- **"New list from this one"** is how the backend says a published list is corrected. The screen creates a draft with the same scope, then copies the rates. Each step has its own idempotency key, so a retry never makes two drafts.
- **Closing asks for the last day in force,** and sends the day after, because the API's `effective_to` is exclusive.
- **Tax rates follow `products.edit`.** RBAC.md §6 has no tax module, and the backend checks `products` on `/tax-rates`.
- **Nothing is ever deleted.** A product is switched off; a list is closed.
- **The mock:** the product master has its own mock with the backend's rules (permissions, idempotency keys, the 409s, slabs, two decimals, forward-only closing). Quotations still price only the six products the quotation mock always had. A product added here lists, gets an HSN code and a rate, but the builder's live pricing doesn't know it. Against the backend both read the same tables.

#### Files changed

- `src/features/products/`: new.
  - `api/`: schemas, API, queries, mutations, and `products.test.ts`.
  - `components/product-master.tsx`: the tabs.
  - `components/product-catalogue.tsx`: the Products tab.
  - `components/product-dialog.tsx`: add and edit, switch off, the HSN section.
  - `components/tax-rates-panel.tsx`: the Tax rates tab.
  - `components/price-lists-panel.tsx`: the Price lists tab, and the new-list and copy form.
  - `components/price-list-sheet.tsx`: the rate sheet, publish and close.
  - `components/pager.tsx`: Previous and Next for offset-paged lists.
  - `components/products-ui.test.tsx`: the UI tests.
  - `hooks/use-product-master-params.ts`: the tab and filters in the URL.
  - `lib/product-labels.ts`: labels, phases, dates and rate checks.
  - `lib/refusals.ts`: refusals in words.
- `src/app/(app)/products/`: the page, and `price-lists/[listId]`, each with a loading state.
- `src/components/layout/navigation.ts`: "Products & prices" under Admin.
- `src/lib/auth/permissions.ts`: the `products` and `pricing` modules.
- `src/mocks/`:
  - `data/products.ts` and `handlers/products.ts`: new;
  - `db.ts`;
  - `handlers/index.ts`;
  - `handlers/quotations.ts`: its `GET /products` moved to the products mock;
  - `data/permissions.ts`: staff can view products and pricing.
- `src/lib/data-ids/registry.ts`, `Docs/Data-IDs.md`: MSTR-004, MSTR-005, MSTR-006.
- `../docs/Backend-Tasks.md`: BE-024.
- `Docs/Plan.md` §9, `Docs/Tested-Features.md`, `Docs/screenshots/products/`: the records.

  - search, and switched-off products;

### Users and roles: people, accounts and leavers

`feature` · `ADMN-001` `ADMN-002` `ADMN-003` `ADMN-004` `ADMN-005` `ADMN-006` · Nakul Srivastava · [entry](changelog/entries/2026-10-10--feature--ADMN-001--users-and-roles-people-accounts-and-leavers.md)

#### Before

The backend has served people administration for a while (`backend/docs/api/users.md`, handover `administration-and-sign-in.md`, twenty-five admin endpoints). On screen, **Admin → Users & roles** was a "Soon" placeholder. Nobody could add a staff member or a dealer's user, reset a password, unlock an account or hand a leaver's leads over without going to the backend.

#### Now

- **Admin → Users & roles** (`/users`, staff with `users`):
  - every staff member and partner user in scope, newest first;
  - each row shows how they sign in, their role, their office or partner, the last sign-in, open leads, and "Deactivated" or "Temporary password";
  - search by name, email or mobile; filter by type, role and status, all in the URL;
  - **Download Excel**, and **New person** for whoever may add people.
- **A person** (`/users/{id}`):
  - **Sign-in:** email or mobile, last sign-in, the password's state, a live lockout with its end, live sessions.
  - **Role and place:** role, office or partner, territories, open leads, and who added them when.
  - **Edit**, and under **More**: set a temporary password, unlock sign-in (while locked out), sign out everywhere, hand over leads and tasks, deactivate or reactivate, delete.
  - **Delete** is disabled while they own open leads, saying to hand over first.
  - **Your own row** is marked "You". It offers no deactivate or delete, and the edit form keeps your role, office and territories read-only, as the backend refuses them.
- **New person** (`/users/new`):
  - **Polysil staff:** name, work email, optional mobile, a staff role (portal roles left out), an open office (searched), territories (added one at a time, removable), and a suggested temporary password that can be regenerated.
  - **Partner user:** name, mobile, partner; their role follows the partner's type.
  - **Once added**, a staff member's temporary password is shown once, with Copy and a reminder to pass it on in person or by phone. Then their page, or another person.
- **Edit** (`/users/{id}/edit`): the same form. Only what changed is sent, and Save stays off until something has.
- **Set a temporary password:** a suggestion or your own (12+ characters). It says how many sessions were signed out, and shows the password once. The person then meets #89's forced change.
- **Hand over:**
  - choose who takes the work over, from those who can work leads;
  - optionally deactivate the leaver once nothing remains;
  - the dialog repeats in batches of 500, each with a new key, while the backend says some remain, then says how many leads and tasks moved.
- **Refusals land where they belong.** A taken email, a short password or a territory role without territories go on their field. The last administrator, or anything else, shows above the buttons.

#### Discussion

**Decisions:**

- **Pages for the form, dialogs for the actions.** Adding or correcting a person is a long form with pickers, so it gets a page. Every account action is a single confirmation, so it gets a dialog that says what happens before it does.
- **A suggested temporary password.** Four groups of four characters with no look-alikes (`Kp7m-Rq4x-Tz9w-Hb3n`), from `crypto.getRandomValues`: over the minimum of 12, and easy to read out by phone. It is shown after saving and never again; the API never returns it.
- **The client's own role and territory rules aren't guessed.** Whether a role needs territories is the backend's answer (`fields.territory_ids`). The form says what territories are for and puts the refusal on the field.
- **The partner picker is the complaints' `DealerPicker`** (any partner type, by name, code or contact person), reused rather than copied.
- **The faded avatar for a deactivated person was dropped.** axe flagged its contrast, and the "Deactivated" badge already says it.

**The mock:**

- People (`mockDb.users`): the signed-in admin (usr-001), the staff who own the mock's leads and tasks, three head-office desks, a deactivated officer, a new joiner with a temporary password, and one user per channel partner.
- Ravi Joshi is locked out for the next few minutes, to show unlock.
- `GET /org-units` (with a closed office) and the sixteen roles of `identity.ASSIGNABLE_ROLES`. The role names and levels are the mock's own.
- The backend's rules:
  - email and mobile unique among live people;
  - a staff role and an open office;
  - territories for the territory roles;
  - nothing changed on your own row;
  - the last administrator kept;
  - delete refused while open leads remain;
  - handover in batches of 500, moving open tasks too;
  - idempotent replays of `POST /users`.

  - `api/users.{schemas,api,queries,mutations}.ts`, with `users.test.ts`;
  - `components/users-list.tsx`, `person-detail.tsx`, `person-dialogs.tsx`, `person-form.tsx`, `person-pages.tsx`, `office-picker.tsx`, with `users-ui.test.tsx`;
  - `hooks/use-user-list-params.ts`, `lib/user-labels.ts`, `lib/temporary-password.ts`.
- `src/app/(app)/users/`: the list, `new`, `[userId]` and `[userId]/edit` routes.

- `src/mocks/data/users.ts`, `src/mocks/handlers/users.ts`: new. `src/mocks/db.ts`, `handlers/index.ts`.
